correctness.rationale: For r>=4 the only non-full resolving neighborhoods are the four-vertex two-page sets and the two cross families involving a spine endpoint. Summing the two-page constraints gives internal weight at least rk/2, and the uniform internal weight k/4 is feasible. At equality the spine weights vanish and every page pair is tight, forcing every page sum to k/2; the cross families then give exactly the stated remaining inequalities. This proves an if-and-only-if optimizer description for every real k in [1,4]. Exact finite replay verifies all neighborhood identities and representative optimum regimes.

value.rationale: The theorem gives the complete optimum polytope for a standard book/Cartesian-product family, distinguishing all equally efficient weighted landmark allocations rather than only their common cost. It exposes genuine structure: uniqueness at r=4 and at maximal redundancy k=4, together with large asymmetric optimum families in another regime. These features are directly relevant to the redundancy interpretation motivating fractional k-metric dimension and are not supplied by the known scalar-value theorems.
